claim: Screening of 367 kinase inhibitors in human neutrophils and a zebrafish tail fin injury model identified ErbBs as common targets of compounds that accelerated inflammation resolution.
source: Screening of 367 kinase inhibitors in human neutrophils and a zebrafish tail fin injury model identified ErbBs as common targets of compounds that accelerated inflammation resolution.
evidence: The abstract states that a screen of 367 kinase inhibitors was performed and identified ErbBs as targets.

claim: The ErbB inhibitors gefitinib, CP-724714, erbstatin and tyrphostin AG825 significantly accelerated apoptosis of human neutrophils.
source: The ErbB inhibitors gefitinib, CP-724714, erbstatin and tyrphostin AG825 significantly accelerated apoptosis of human neutrophils, including neutrophils from people with COPD.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states these compounds accelerated neutrophil apoptosis, supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: ErbB inhibitors significantly accelerated apoptosis of neutrophils from people with COPD.
source: The ErbB inhibitors gefitinib, CP-724714, erbstatin and tyrphostin AG825 significantly accelerated apoptosis of human neutrophils, including neutrophils from people with COPD.
evidence: The abstract and Figure 2E-F show that erbstatin and tyrphostin AG825 increased apoptosis in COPD patient neutrophils.

claim: Neutrophil apoptosis was increased in Tyrphostin AG825 treated-zebrafish in vivo.
source: Neutrophil apoptosis was also increased in Tyrphostin AG825 treated-zebrafish in vivo.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by data in Figure 6H-I showing increased apoptotic neutrophils.

claim: Tyrphostin AG825 decreased peritoneal inflammation in zymosan-treated mice.
source: Tyrphostin AG825 decreased peritoneal inflammation in zymosan-treated mice, and increased lung neutrophil apoptosis and macrophage efferocytosis in a murine acute lung injury model.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by data in Figure 5G showing reduced cell counts in peritoneal lavage.

claim: Tyrphostin AG825 increased lung neutrophil apoptosis in a murine acute lung injury model.
source: Tyrphostin AG825 decreased peritoneal inflammation in zymosan-treated mice, and increased lung neutrophil apoptosis and macrophage efferocytosis in a murine acute lung injury model.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by data in Figure 5C showing increased neutrophil apoptosis in BAL.

claim: Tyrphostin AG825 increased macrophage efferocytosis in a murine acute lung injury model.
source: Tyrphostin AG825 decreased peritoneal inflammation in zymosan-treated mice, and increased lung neutrophil apoptosis and macrophage efferocytosis in a murine acute lung injury model.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by data in Figure 5D showing increased macrophage efferocytosis.

claim: Tyrphostin AG825 reduced inflammation in zebrafish.
source: Tyrphostin AG825 and knockdown of egfra and erbb2 by CRISPR/Cas9 reduced inflammation in zebrafish.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by data in Figure 6B showing reduced neutrophils at injury site.

claim: Knockdown of egfra and erbb2 by CRISPR/Cas9 reduced inflammation in zebrafish.
source: Tyrphostin AG825 and knockdown of egfra and erbb2 by CRISPR/Cas9 reduced inflammation in zebrafish.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by data in Figure 6D showing reduced neutrophils at injury site in crispants.

claim: Inhibitors of ErbB kinases have therapeutic potential in neutrophilic inflammatory disease.
source: Our work shows that inhibitors of ErbB kinases have therapeutic potential in neutrophilic inflammatory disease.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, based on the collective experimental findings.

claim: Neutrophilic inflammation is central to chronic inflammatory diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
source: Neutrophilic inflammation is central to chronic inflammatory diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), which impose an increasing social and economic burden on our aging population.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about inflammatory diseases.

claim: Treatment of COPD by next-generation combination therapy with inhaled corticosteroids and newer bronchodilators are viewed as maintenance pharmacotherapies but they do not specifically target cellular inflammation.
source: Treatment of COPD by next-generation combination therapy with inhaled corticosteroids and newer bronchodilators are viewed as maintenance pharmacotherapies but they do not specifically target cellular inflammation.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of current COPD therapies.

claim: The anti-inflammatory phosphodiesterase-4 inhibitor, roflumilast, targets systemic inflammation associated with COPD and reduces moderate to severe exacerbations in severe disease.
source: The anti-inflammatory phosphodiesterase-4 inhibitor, roflumilast, targets systemic inflammation associated with COPD and reduces moderate to severe exacerbations in severe disease, possibly via effects on eosinophils (Martinez et al., 2018; Rabe et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Martinez et al., 2018 and Rabe et al., 2018.

claim: In chronic inflammatory diseases, clearance of neutrophils by apoptosis is dysregulated particularly during exacerbations.
source: In these diseases, clearance of neutrophils by apoptosis is dysregulated particularly during exacerbations (Pletz et al., 2004; Sapey et al., 2011), but to date it has not been possible to therapeutically modify this, indeed corticosteroids can supress neutrophil apoptosis and hence perpetuate inflammation (Liles et al., 1995).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Pletz et al., 2004 and Sapey et al., 2011.

claim: Corticosteroids can suppress neutrophil apoptosis and hence perpetuate inflammation.
source: In these diseases, clearance of neutrophils by apoptosis is dysregulated particularly during exacerbations (Pletz et al., 2004; Sapey et al., 2011), but to date it has not been possible to therapeutically modify this, indeed corticosteroids can supress neutrophil apoptosis and hence perpetuate inflammation (Liles et al., 1995).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Liles et al., 1995.

claim: Neutrophil persistence in tissues, caused by a delay in apoptosis, can result in a destructive cellular phenotype.
source: Neutrophil persistence in tissues, caused by a delay in apoptosis, can result in a destructive cellular phenotype, whereby neutrophils have greater potential to expel histotoxic factors such as proteases and oxidative molecules onto surrounding tissue.
evidence: This is stated as a mechanistic understanding of neutrophil-mediated tissue damage.

claim: In COPD, delayed apoptosis is considered to be a key part of the pathogenesis.
source: In COPD, among other diseases, delayed apoptosis is considered to be a key part of the pathogenesis, occurring either as a result of pro-survival factors that are present in the lung microenvironment or an innate apoptosis defect (Brown et al., 2009; Haslett, 1999; Pletz et al., 2004; Zhang et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Brown et al., 2009; Haslett, 1999; Pletz et al., 2004; Zhang et al., 2012.

claim: There are no effective treatment strategies in clinical use to specifically reverse delayed neutrophil apoptosis.
source: Despite this mechanistic understanding, there are no effective treatment strategies in clinical use to specifically reverse this cellular mechanism.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in current clinical practice.

claim: Accelerating neutrophil apoptosis has been shown to promote the resolution of inflammation in multiple experimental models.
source: Accelerating neutrophil apoptosis has been shown to promote the resolution of inflammation in multiple experimental models (Burgon et al., 2014; Chello et al., 2007; Ren et al., 2008; Rossi et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Burgon et al., 2014; Chello et al., 2007; Ren et al., 2008; Rossi et al., 2006.

claim: Protein kinases are important in regulating neutrophil apoptosis.
source: A number of studies highlight the importance of protein kinases in regulating neutrophil apoptosis (Burgon et al., 2014; Rossi et al., 2006; Webb et al., 2000) and therefore reveal potential therapeutically targetable pathways for inflammatory disease.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Burgon et al., 2014; Rossi et al., 2006; Webb et al., 2000.

claim: The ErbB family consist of four RTKs with structural homology to the human epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR/ErbB1/Her-1).
source: The ErbB family consist of four RTKs with structural homology to the human epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR/ErbB1/Her-1).
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge about the ErbB family.

claim: The screen identified 16 hit compounds which reduced neutrophil number at the site of injury in the zebrafish model.
source: The screen identified 16 hit compounds which reduced neutrophil number at the site of injury in the zebrafish model (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: ABL1, PDGFRα, PDGFRβ, p38α and ErbB4 were the top five most frequently targeted kinases overall in the zebrafish screen.
source: A number of kinases were inhibited by the 16 compounds, with Abelson murine leukaemia viral homolog 1 (ABL1), Platelet-derived growth factor receptor (PDGFR) α, PDGFRβ, p38α and ErbB4 being the top five most frequently targeted kinases overall.
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing the zebrafish screen outcomes.

claim: The most selective compounds in the zebrafish screen targeted the kinases YES, ABL1, p38 and the ErbB family.
source: The most selective compounds, that is those that strongly inhibited individual kinases or kinase families, targeted the kinases YES, ABL1, p38 and the ErbB family.
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing the zebrafish screen outcomes.

claim: PKIS screening at 62 µM resulted in 62 compounds that accelerated neutrophil apoptosis ≥2 fold compared to DMSO control.
source: PKIS compounds were screened at 62 µM in order to maximise the chance of identifying 'hits' and resulted in 62 compounds that accelerated neutrophil apoptosis ≥2 fold compared to DMSO control (Figure 1B and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Secondary screening of top 38 compounds at 10 µM yielded 11 compounds that accelerated neutrophil apoptosis ≥2 fold over control.
source: Secondary screening of top 38 compounds (chosen from the 62 hits based on greatest selectivity for kinase targets) was carried out at 10 µM in order to reduce false positives. This yielded 11 compounds that accelerated neutrophil apoptosis ≥2 fold over control (as indicated by dashed green line, Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Kinases targeted by the 11 hit compounds included DYRK1B, KIT, EGFR, ErbB2 and ErbB4, PDGFR, CDK6 and p38.
source: Kinases targeted by these compounds included DYRK1B, KIT, EGFR, ErbB2 and ErbB4, PDGFR, CDK6 and p38 (Figure 1C, inset).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1C inset table.

claim: Members of the ErbB family of RTKs were the most frequently inhibited kinase family after known regulators of neutrophil survival (p38, PI3K).
source: The identification of known regulators of neutrophil survival (p38, PI3K) was encouraging support for the screen design and execution. We found that members of the ErbB family of RTKs were the next most frequently inhibited kinase family, being targeted by three highly selective compounds out of the 11 hits (Figure 1C, inset).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Gefitinib is the most effective clinically used ErbB inhibitor in promoting neutrophil apoptosis, reaching significance at 50 µM.
source: We show that among inhibitors of ErbBs that are in clinical use, the EGFR inhibitor, gefitinib, is the most effective in promoting neutrophil apoptosis, reaching significance at 50 µM (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: CP-724714 promoted neutrophil apoptosis in a dose-dependent manner.
source: The ErbB2-selective inhibitor, CP-724714 (Jani et al., 2007) also promoted neutrophil apoptosis in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2B) as did Erbstatin and tyrphostin AG825, selective for EGFR and ErbB2 respectively (Osherov et al., 1993; Umezawa and Imoto, 1991) (Figure 2C–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2B, with citation to Jani et al., 2007.

claim: Erbstatin promoted neutrophil apoptosis in a dose-dependent manner.
source: The ErbB2-selective inhibitor, CP-724714 (Jani et al., 2007) also promoted neutrophil apoptosis in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2B) as did Erbstatin and tyrphostin AG825, selective for EGFR and ErbB2 respectively (Osherov et al., 1993; Umezawa and Imoto, 1991) (Figure 2C–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2C, with citations to Osherov et al., 1993 and Umezawa and Imoto, 1991.

claim: Tyrphostin AG825 promoted neutrophil apoptosis in a dose-dependent manner.
source: The ErbB2-selective inhibitor, CP-724714 (Jani et al., 2007) also promoted neutrophil apoptosis in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2B) as did Erbstatin and tyrphostin AG825, selective for EGFR and ErbB2 respectively (Osherov et al., 1993; Umezawa and Imoto, 1991) (Figure 2C–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2D, with citations to Osherov et al., 1993 and Umezawa and Imoto, 1991.

claim: The pan-caspase inhibitor Q-VD-OPh completely abrogated Erbstatin and tyrphostin AG825-driven neutrophil apoptosis.
source: Furthermore, the pan-caspase inhibitor Q-VD-OPh (Wardle et al., 2011) completely abrogated Erbstatin and tyrphostin AG825-driven neutrophil apoptosis, confirming the caspase dependence of inhibitor mediated cell death (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D–E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D–E, with citation to Wardle et al., 2011.

claim: Erbstatin and tyrphostin AG825 significantly increased apoptosis of neutrophils from both COPD patients and healthy control subjects in a dose dependent manner at 6 hr.
source: Erbstatin and tyrphostin AG825 significantly increased apoptosis of neutrophils from both COPD patients and healthy control subjects in a dose dependent manner at both 6 hr (Figure 2E–F) and 20 hr (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2E-F.

claim: Factors that raise intracellular cAMP concentration are present during inflammation and prolong neutrophil survival via activation of cAMP-dependent protein kinases.
source: Factors that raise intracellular cAMP concentration ([cAMP]i) are present during inflammation, and elevated [cAMP]i is known to prolong neutrophil survival via activation of cAMP-dependent protein kinases (Krakstad et al., 2004; Vaughan et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Krakstad et al., 2004 and Vaughan et al., 2007.

claim: Neutrophil apoptosis was reduced by N6-MB-cAMP, and this was reversed by Erbstatin analog and Tyrphostin AG825.
source: We show that neutrophil apoptosis was reduced by the cAMP analogue and site selective activator of PKA, N6-monobutyryl-cAMP (N6-MB-cAMP), and that this was reversed by Erbstatin analog (Figure 3A) and Tyrphostin AG825 (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3A-B.

claim: Erbstatin and tyrphostin AG825 prevent GMCSF-mediated survival in COPD and age-matched healthy control neutrophils.
source: We show that erbstatin and tyrphostin AG825 prevent GMCSF-mediated survival in COPD and age-matched healthy control neutrophils (Figure 3D–E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3D-E.

claim: GMCSF is known to promote neutrophil survival via the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/AKT pathway, ultimately leading to the stabilisation of the anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 family member, Mcl-1.
source: GMCSF is known to promote neutrophil survival via the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/AKT pathway, ultimately leading to the stabilisation of the anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 family member, Mcl-1 (Derouet et al., 2004; Klein et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Derouet et al., 2004 and Klein et al., 2000.

claim: Tyrphostin AG825 reduced GMCSF-induced AKT phosphorylation after 15 and 30 min of treatment becoming statistically significant at 15 mins.
source: To investigate potential mechanisms underpinning the ability of tyrphostin AG825 to prevent GMCSF-mediated survival, we assessed AKT-phosphorylation as a measure of PI3K activation and found that tyrphostin AG825 reduced GMCSF-induced AKT phosphorylation after 15 and 30 min of treatment becoming statistically significant at 15 mins (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Tyrphostin AG825 accelerated the spontaneous downregulation of Mcl-1 and prevented GMCSF-induced stabilisation of Mcl-1.
source: Tyrphostin AG825 accelerated the spontaneous downregulation of Mcl-1 and also prevented GMCSF-induced stabilisation of Mcl-1 (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3G.

claim: ErbB2 phosphorylation was detected at 30 min (1.94 > control) and 60 min (1.53 > control) in neutrophils stimulated with N6-MB-cAMP.
source: Among these targets, ErbB2 phosphorylation was detected at 30 min (1.94 > control) and 60 min (1.53 > control, Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Table 1.

claim: ErbB2 mRNA was detected in human neutrophils by RT-PCR.
source: In support of this, we detected the presence of ErbB2 mRNA in human neutrophils by RT-PCR (Figure 4A) and a 60kD protein (lower molecular weight ErbB family products are well-documented (Jackson et al., 2013; Guillaudeau et al., 2012; Siegel, 1999; Ward et al., 2013) which was upregulated by GMCSF and dbcAMP (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4A, with citations to Jackson et al., 2013; Guillaudeau et al., 2012; Siegel, 1999; Ward et al., 2013.

claim: A 60kD ErbB2 protein was detected in human neutrophils which was upregulated by GMCSF and dbcAMP.
source: In support of this, we detected the presence of ErbB2 mRNA in human neutrophils by RT-PCR (Figure 4A) and a 60kD protein (lower molecular weight ErbB family products are well-documented (Jackson et al., 2013; Guillaudeau et al., 2012; Siegel, 1999; Ward et al., 2013) which was upregulated by GMCSF and dbcAMP (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4B, with citations to Jackson et al., 2013; Guillaudeau et al., 2012; Siegel, 1999; Ward et al., 2013.

claim: ErbB3 was detected in human neutrophils by ELISA.
source: ErbB3 was also detected in human neutrophils by ELISA (Figure 4C), at levels similar to those observed in other tissues in literature (Buta et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4C, with citation to Buta et al., 2016.

claim: Tyrphostin AG825 had no effect on percentage of, or absolute number of neutrophils or macrophages in BAL compared to DMSO control in LPS-induced airway inflammation.
source: Tyrphostin AG825 had no effect on percentage of, or absolute number of neutrophils or macrophages compared to DMSO control (Figure 5A–B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5A-B.

claim: Tyrphostin AG825 significantly increased the percentage of neutrophil apoptosis in murine LPS-induced airway inflammation.
source: Tyrphostin AG825 significantly increased the percentage of neutrophil apoptosis, both visualised as 'free' apoptotic cells (closed circles) and as a summation of both free apoptotic cells and apoptotic inclusions within macrophages in order to capture those that had been efferocytosed (closed triangles, Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Macrophage efferocytosis was significantly elevated by tyrphostin AG825 compared to vehicle control in murine LPS-induced airway inflammation.
source: Macrophage efferocytosis was also significantly elevated by tyrphostin AG825, compared to vehicle control (Figure 5D), determined by counting the number of macrophages containing apoptotic inclusions as a proportion of total macrophages (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5D-E.

claim: Tyrphostin AG825 does not induce leukopenia.
source: Importantly, tyrphostin AG825 does not induce leukopenia (Figure 5F), however significantly fewer inflammatory cells were found in peritoneal lavage following tyrphostin AG825 treatment (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Significantly fewer inflammatory cells were found in peritoneal lavage following tyrphostin AG825 treatment in zymosan-induced peritonitis.
source: Importantly, tyrphostin AG825 does not induce leukopenia (Figure 5F), however significantly fewer inflammatory cells were found in peritoneal lavage following tyrphostin AG825 treatment (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5G.

claim: The neutrophil chemoattractant and proinflammatory cytokine, KC, was reduced in tyrphostin AG825 treated mice in zymosan-induced peritonitis.
source: The neutrophil chemoattractant and proinflammatory cytokine, KC, was reduced in tyrphostin AG825 treated mice, and concomitant with this, a trend for less IL-6 was also observed (Figure 5H).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5H.

claim: IgM is significantly reduced in tyrphostin AG825-treated mice in zymosan-induced peritonitis.
source: IgM, which correlates with the number and activation of peritoneal B lymphocytes (Almeida et al., 2001), is significantly reduced in tyrphostin AG825-treated mice (Figure 5I).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5I, with citation to Almeida et al., 2001.

claim: Tyrphostin AG825 significantly reduced the number of neutrophils at the site of injury at 4 and 8 hpi in zebrafish tail fin injury model.
source: In the mpx:GFP zebrafish tail fin injury model (Renshaw et al., 2006) (Figure 6A) we were able to show that tyrphostin AG825 (Figure 6B) and CP-724714 (Figure 6C) significantly reduced the number of neutrophils at the site of injury at 4 and 8 hpi.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6B, with citation to Renshaw et al., 2006.

claim: CP-724714 significantly reduced the number of neutrophils at the site of injury at 4 and 8 hpi in zebrafish tail fin injury model.
source: In the mpx:GFP zebrafish tail fin injury model (Renshaw et al., 2006) (Figure 6A) we were able to show that tyrphostin AG825 (Figure 6B) and CP-724714 (Figure 6C) significantly reduced the number of neutrophils at the site of injury at 4 and 8 hpi.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6C, with citation to Renshaw et al., 2006.

claim: Simultaneous gene knockdown of egfra and erbb2 via CRISPR/Cas9 reduced the number of neutrophils at the site of injury in zebrafish.
source: Simultaneous gene knockdown of egfra and erbb2 via CRISPR/Cas9 (referred to as 'crispants') also recapitulated this phenotype (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Tyrphostin AG825 did not affect total neutrophil number in zebrafish.
source: Tyrphostin AG825 did not affect total neutrophil number (Figure 6E), but egfra and erbb2 crispants had significantly fewer neutrophils (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6E.

claim: egfra and erbb2 crispants had significantly fewer total neutrophils in zebrafish.
source: Tyrphostin AG825 did not affect total neutrophil number (Figure 6E), but egfra and erbb2 crispants had significantly fewer neutrophils (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Tyrphostin AG825 upregulated neutrophil apoptosis at the site of injury in zebrafish.
source: As demonstrated by TSA and TUNEL double staining (Figure 6G), tyrphostin AG825 upregulated neutrophil apoptosis at both the site of injury (Figure 6H) and in the caudal hematopoietic tissue (CHT) of zebrafish (Figure 6I).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6G-H.

claim: Tyrphostin AG825 upregulated neutrophil apoptosis in the caudal hematopoietic tissue (CHT) of zebrafish.
source: As demonstrated by TSA and TUNEL double staining (Figure 6G), tyrphostin AG825 upregulated neutrophil apoptosis at both the site of injury (Figure 6H) and in the caudal hematopoietic tissue (CHT) of zebrafish (Figure 6I).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6G and 6I.

claim: Promoting neutrophil apoptosis is a desirable approach for the resolution of inflammation, since apoptosis functionally downregulates the cell, promotes rapid cell clearance by efferocytosis and engages an anti-inflammatory phenotype in phagocytosing cells.
source: Promoting neutrophil apoptosis is a desirable approach for the resolution of inflammation, since apoptosis functionally downregulates the cell, promotes rapid cell clearance by efferocytosis and engages an anti-inflammatory phenotype in phagocytosing cells (Savill et al., 1989; Whyte et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Savill et al., 1989 and Whyte et al., 1999.

claim: Several compounds targeting the ErbB family have been approved as medicines for the treatment of cancer.
source: Several compounds targeting the ErbB family have been approved as medicines for the treatment of cancer (Singh et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Singh et al., 2016.

claim: The ErbB family are critical regulators of cell proliferation and are associated with the development of many human malignancies.
source: The ErbB family are critical regulators of cell proliferation and are associated with the development of many human malignancies (Roskoski, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Roskoski, 2014.

claim: ErbB members have known roles in inflammatory diseases of the airway, skin and gut.
source: In addition to the development of cancer, ErbB members have known roles in inflammatory diseases of the airway, skin and gut (Davies et al., 1999; Finigan et al., 2011; Frey and Brent Polk, 2014; Hamilton et al., 2003; Pastore et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Davies et al., 1999; Finigan et al., 2011; Frey and Brent Polk, 2014; Hamilton et al., 2003; Pastore et al., 2008.

claim: ErbB2 is upregulated in whole lung lysates in murine bleomycin models of lung injury.
source: In the context of lung inflammation, ErbB2 is upregulated in whole lung lysates in murine bleomycin models of lung injury and EGFR ligands are increased in BAL from acute lung injury patients receiving mechanical ventilation (Finigan et al., 2011), suggesting ErbB signalling axes may play a role in the process of airway inflammation in vivo.
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Finigan et al., 2011.

claim: EGFR ligands are increased in BAL from acute lung injury patients receiving mechanical ventilation.
source: In the context of lung inflammation, ErbB2 is upregulated in whole lung lysates in murine bleomycin models of lung injury and EGFR ligands are increased in BAL from acute lung injury patients receiving mechanical ventilation (Finigan et al., 2011), suggesting ErbB signalling axes may play a role in the process of airway inflammation in vivo.
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Finigan et al., 2011.

claim: The benefit of EGFR inhibitors in reducing inflammation in ventilator-induced and OVA/LPS-induced lung injury rodent models is shown by others.
source: The benefit of EGFR inhibitors in reducing inflammation in ventilator-induced and OVA/LPS-induced lung injury rodent models is shown by others, further supporting the targetting of this pathway in inflammatory disease settings (Bierman et al., 2008; Shimizu et al., 2018; Takezawa et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Bierman et al., 2008; Shimizu et al., 2018; Takezawa et al., 2016.

claim: Neutrophils express members of the ErbB family.
source: Others have reported that neutrophils express members of the ErbB family (Lewkowicz et al., 2005), particularly ErbB2 at low levels (Petryszak et al., 2016) and we show that they are phosphorylated and regulated following exposure to inflammatory stimuli.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Lewkowicz et al., 2005 and Petryszak et al., 2016.

claim: ErbBs have known roles in suppressing apoptosis of epithelial cells and keratinocytes.
source: ErbBs have known roles in suppressing apoptosis of epithelial cells and keratinocytes, but this study is the first to show a role for ErbBs in survival signalling of myeloid cells.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the discussion.

claim: This study is the first to show a role for ErbBs in survival signalling of myeloid cells.
source: ErbBs have known roles in suppressing apoptosis of epithelial cells and keratinocytes, but this study is the first to show a role for ErbBs in survival signalling of myeloid cells.
evidence: This is stated as a novel finding of the current study.

claim: Erbstatin has been shown to inhibit neutrophil ROS production.
source: Erbstatin has been shown to inhibit neutrophil ROS production (Dreiem et al., 2003; Mócsai et al., 1997; Reistad et al., 2005) and chemotactic responses (Yasui et al., 1994).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Dreiem et al., 2003; Mócsai et al., 1997; Reistad et al., 2005.

claim: Erbstatin has been shown to inhibit neutrophil chemotactic responses.
source: Erbstatin has been shown to inhibit neutrophil ROS production (Dreiem et al., 2003; Mócsai et al., 1997; Reistad et al., 2005) and chemotactic responses (Yasui et al., 1994).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Yasui et al., 1994.

claim: Cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs) play a role in neutrophil survival and neutrophilic inflammation.
source: Other kinase families have been found to play a role in neutrophil survival and neutrophilic inflammation, most notably the cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs) (Rossi et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Rossi et al., 2006.

claim: Compounds targeting CDKs were identified as drivers of neutrophil apoptosis in both primary and secondary screens.
source: In accordance with this, compounds targeting CDKs were identified as drivers of neutrophil apoptosis in both our primary and secondary screens.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the screening experiments.

claim: p38 MAPK inhibitor compounds were identified in both zebrafish and human screens.
source: Moreover, p38 MAPK inhibitor compounds were also identified in both zebrafish and human screens, and since this kinase is known to mediate survival signals, these findings give confidence to the robustness of the screen design and execution.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the screening experiments.

claim: p38 MAPK is known to mediate survival signals in neutrophils.
source: Moreover, p38 MAPK inhibitor compounds were also identified in both zebrafish and human screens, and since this kinase is known to mediate survival signals, these findings give confidence to the robustness of the screen design and execution.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Inhibiting ErbBs as a therapeutic strategy may achieve an overall anti-inflammatory effect in in vivo systems, facilitating clearance by macrophages.
source: This suggests that inhibiting ErbBs as a therapeutic strategy may achieve an overall anti-inflammatory effect in in vivo systems, facilitating clearance by macrophages.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the experimental findings.

claim: There was no evidence of secondary neutrophil necrosis due to overwhelming macrophage clearance capacity following tyrphostin AG825 treatment.
source: In support of this, we provide evidence of increased efferocytosis in vivo following tyrphostin AG825 treatment, with no evidence of secondary neutrophil necrosis due to overwhelming macrophage clearance capacity, evidenced both morphologically and by TO-PRO-3 staining.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the experimental data.

claim: Erbstatin can prevent GMCSF-mediated activation of PI3K in human neutrophils.
source: Others have shown the ability of erbstatin to prevent GMCSF-mediated activation of PI3K in human neutrophils, although the impact on cell survival was not studied (al-Shami et al., 1997).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to al-Shami et al., 1997.

claim: ErbBs may function as an early and upstream component of the survival pathway in neutrophils.
source: Therefore, ErbBs may function as an early and upstream component of the survival pathway in neutrophils.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the experimental findings on AKT phosphorylation.

claim: Unlike all other ErbBs, ErbB2 monomers exist in a constitutively active conformation and can form homodimers that do not require a ligand for activation.
source: Unlike all other ErbBs, ErbB2 monomers exist in a constitutively active conformation and can form homodimers that do not require a ligand for activation (Fan et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Fan et al., 2008.

claim: ErbBs activate multiple components including those known to be critical in neutrophil cell survival such as PI3K, MAPK and GSK-3.
source: ErbBs achieve great signalling diversity: in part because of the individual biochemical properties of ligands and multiple homo-heterodimer combinations, and in part because they activate multiple components including those known to be critical in neutrophil cell survival such as PI3K, MAPK and GSK-3, as well as phosphorylating the Bcl-2 protein Bad which inhibits its death-promoting activity (Yarden and Sliwkowski, 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Yarden and Sliwkowski, 2001.

claim: ErbBs phosphorylate the Bcl-2 protein Bad which inhibits its death-promoting activity.
source: ErbBs achieve great signalling diversity: in part because of the individual biochemical properties of ligands and multiple homo-heterodimer combinations, and in part because they activate multiple components including those known to be critical in neutrophil cell survival such as PI3K, MAPK and GSK-3, as well as phosphorylating the Bcl-2 protein Bad which inhibits its death-promoting activity (Yarden and Sliwkowski, 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Yarden and Sliwkowski, 2001.

claim: Mammalian models of ErbB deletion are limited by profound abnormalities in utero and during development.
source: Mammalian models of ErbB deletion are limited by profound abnormalities in utero and during development (Britsch et al., 1998; Dackor et al., 2007; Gassmann et al., 1995; Miettinen et al., 1995; Riethmacher et al., 1997).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Britsch et al., 1998; Dackor et al., 2007; Gassmann et al., 1995; Miettinen et al., 1995; Riethmacher et al., 1997.

claim: Targeting ErbBs genetically and pharmacologically reduces the number of neutrophils at the site of injury in zebrafish.
source: Targeting ErbBs genetically and pharmacologically reduces the number of neutrophils at the site of injury in zebrafish, which may reflect inhibition of a number of pathways that regulate neutrophil number in the tissue, including migration pathways (Ellett et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the zebrafish experiments, with citation to Ellett et al., 2015.

claim: The increase in apoptotic neutrophil count at the site of injury with ErbB inhibitor treatment suggests ErbBs may be inducing anti-apoptotic signalling pathways within this inflammatory environment.
source: However, the increase in apoptotic neutrophil count at the site of injury with ErbB inhibitor treatment suggests ErbBs may be inducing anti-apoptotic signalling pathways within this inflammatory environment, which could at least in part be causing the phenotype.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The reduced neutrophil count at the injury site may be due to the increase in apoptotic neutrophils in the CHT, which may be preventing neutrophil migration to sites of injury.
source: The reduced neutrophil count at the injury site may also be due to the increase in apoptotic neutrophils in the CHT, which may be preventing neutrophil migration to sites of injury.
evidence: This is stated as a possible explanation for the observed phenotype.

claim: The unchanged whole body neutrophil number with tyrphostin AG825 treatment is potentially due to compensatory upregulation of neutrophil production within the CHT.
source: The unchanged whole body neutrophil number is potentially due to compensatory upregulation of neutrophil production within the CHT.
evidence: This is stated as a possible explanation for the observed phenotype.

claim: Genetic deletion of egfra and erbb2 significantly reduced whole body neutrophil number in zebrafish.
source: Genetic deletion, but not pharmacological inhibition, of egfra and erbb2 significantly reduced whole body neutrophil number, which may reflect crispants being without egfra and erbb2 genes from a one-cell stage.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the zebrafish experiments.

claim: Reduced neutrophils at the injury site of crispants may be explained by their reduced whole body neutrophil number and potentially defects in the migratory response of these neutrophils to a site of inflammation.
source: Reduced neutrophils at the injury site of crispants may be explained by their reduced whole body neutrophil number, but potentially also defects in the migratory response of these neutrophils to a site of inflammation.
evidence: This is stated as a possible explanation for the observed phenotype.

claim: The average mutation rate in egfra erbb2 crispants was 97.5% for egfra and 87.9% for erbb2.
source: The average mutation rate in our experiments was 97.5% and 87.9% for egfra and erbb2, respectively.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the genotyping experiments.

claim: Total cell counts in peritoneal lavage were 2.2 × 10^6 in PBS vs 1.7 × 10^7 in zymosan treated animals at 4 hr.
source: Total cell counts in peritoneal lavage were 2.2 × 106 in PBS vs 1.7 × 107 in zymosan treated animals at 4 hr demonstrating established inflammation at this time point (Navarro-Xavier et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as a result from the peritonitis experiments, with citation to Navarro-Xavier et al., 2010.

claim: C57BL/6 mice nebulised with LPS developed an acute pulmonary neutrophilia after 48 hr.
source: C57BL/6 mice nebulised with LPS developed an acute pulmonary neutrophilia after 48 hr, to a degree seen previously (Figure 5A–B) (Thompson et al., 2014).
